text.en: Believing Type Ia supernovae are useful as standard candles just because they are generally bright, with no deeper reason for their consistency — their usefulness comes specifically from always detonating at nearly the same mass (the Chandrasekhar limit), which gives them a remarkably consistent intrinsic peak brightness, unlike core-collapse supernovae whose brightness varies with the original star's properties.
text.et: Arvamus, et I tüüpi supernoovad on standardküünaldena kasulikud lihtsalt seetõttu, et need on üldiselt heledad, ilma sügavama põhjuseta nende ühtluse jaoks — nende kasulikkus tuleb spetsiifiliselt sellest, et need plahvatavad alati peaaegu samal massil (Chandrasekhari piiril), mis annab neile märkimisväärselt ühtlase tegeliku tippheleduse, erinevalt tuuma kokkuvarisemise supernoovadest, mille heledus varieerub algse tähe omadustega.
